hypotheses.justification: Proof: split on `ϖ ^ 3 ∣ W.a₆`. If it holds, the existing proof applies. If not, `tateCubicRoots` is empty. Suppose t = mk t₀ with ϖ⁴ ∣ (ϖt₀)³ + a₂(ϖt₀)² + a₄(ϖt₀) + a₆. By h₂ and h₄, ϖ³ divides each of the first three terms (ϖ³t₀³, ϖ·ϖ²t₀², ϖ²·ϖt₀). Since ϖ³ ∣ ϖ⁴, `dvd_sub` gives ϖ³ ∣ a₆, a contradiction. So `Nat.card` is 0 ≤ 3. This argument needs h₂ and h₄, so h₆ can be deleted only on its own.

Proof: split on `ϖ ^ 2 ∣ W.a₄`. If it holds, the existing proof applies. If not, `tateCubicRoots ⊆ {0}`. Suppose t = mk t₀ with ϖ⁴ ∣ g(t₀). By h₂ and h₆, ϖ³ divides ϖ³t₀³, a₂ϖ²t₀² and a₆, so ϖ³ ∣ ϖ·(a₄t₀). Cancel ϖ, which is allowed because R is a domain and ϖ ≠ 0 (`mul_dvd_mul_iff_left`). This gives ϖ² ∣ a₄t₀. Now assume ϖ ∤ t₀. Since ϖ is prime, ϖ ∣ a₄, so a₄ = ϖc. Then ϖ² ∣ ϖct₀, so ϖ ∣ ct₀, so ϖ ∣ c, so ϖ² ∣ a₄, a contradiction. Hence ϖ ∣ t₀, and t = mk t₀ = 0 by `Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem` and `Ideal.mem_span_singleton`. Then `Nat.card` ≤ ncard {0} = 1 ≤ 3, using `Nat.card_coe_set_eq`, `Set.ncard_le_ncard` and `Set.ncard_singleton`. This argument needs h₂ and h₆, so h₄ can be deleted only on its own.

Proof: split on `ϖ ∣ W.a₂`. If it holds, the existing proof applies. If not, `tateCubicRoots ⊆ {0}`. Suppose t = mk t₀ with ϖ⁴ ∣ (ϖt₀)³ + a₂(ϖt₀)² + a₄(ϖt₀) + a₆. By h₄ and h₆, ϖ³ divides ϖ³t₀³, a₄ϖt₀ and a₆, so ϖ³ ∣ ϖ²·(a₂t₀²). Cancel ϖ² using `mul_dvd_mul_iff_left` (R is a domain and ϖ ≠ 0), giving ϖ ∣ a₂t₀². Since ϖ is prime and ϖ ∤ a₂, ϖ ∣ t₀², so ϖ ∣ t₀ by `Prime.dvd_of_dvd_pow`. Hence mk t₀ = 0, and `Nat.card` ≤ ncard {0} = 1 ≤ 3, using `Nat.card_coe_set_eq`, `Set.ncard_le_ncard` and `Set.ncard_singleton`. This argument needs h₄ and h₆, so h₂ can be deleted only on its own; I did not check whether two of h₂, h₄, h₆ can be deleted at once.
